title: acer orientale subsp. syriacum
intro: Acer orientale subsp. syriacum, commonly known as the Syrian maple, is a subspecies of the Oriental maple tree, native to the mountainous regions of Western Asia. The health benefits of the Syrian maple include its use in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of this plant are attributed to its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which contribute to its potential in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of the Syrian maple include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been shown to exhibit antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
